descriptors.concept_name: Selection of Accounting Policy in Absence of Specific Standard
descriptors.definition: When no specific Ind AS governs a transaction, management uses its judgment to develop an accounting policy ensuring the resulting information is relevant to economic decisions and faithfully represents financial position, performance, and cash flows. The chosen policy must reflect economic substance over legal form while remaining neutral, prudent, and complete.
inclusion: Transactions or conditions not explicitly covered by existing Ind AS
Policies developed via management judgment reflecting economic substance
exclusion: Transactions explicitly addressed by an existing specific Ind AS
nearby_distinctions: Differs from applying a clear existing standard; applies only when a regulatory gap exists for new business models or technologies.

descriptors.definition: Entities must select and apply accounting policies consistently for similar transactions, events, and conditions unless an explicit standard requires or permits categorization. Maintaining consistency ensures that financial results across different periods remain comparable and reflect a true and fair financial position.
inclusion: Uniform application of cost formulas or valuation models across similar asset classes
Categorized items permitted by specific Ind AS to use different policies
exclusion: Arbitrary or year-to-year shifts in accounting bases without standard justification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from changes in accounting policies, which are strictly restricted unless mandated or proven to provide more relevant and reliable information.

descriptors.definition: An entity is restricted from altering its established accounting policies unless the change is mandated by an accounting standard or produces more reliable and relevant information for users. Frequent or arbitrary shifts are disallowed to preserve the temporal comparability of financial statements and trends.
inclusion: Changes required by a new or revised Ind AS
Voluntary modifications providing enhanced relevance and reliability
exclusion: Initial adoption of policies for transactions previously immaterial or non-existent
Adoption of a new policy for events differing in substance
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from changes in accounting estimates, which arise from new information or changing circumstances rather than a modification of foundational accounting principles.

descriptors.concept_name: Disclosure Regarding the Changes in Accounting Policies
descriptors.definition: When an initial standard application or a voluntary policy change affects current, prior, or future periods, the entity must disclose comprehensive details including the nature of the change, transitional provisions, and line-item adjustments. If retrospective application is impracticable, the circumstances and operational application method must be explicitly stated.
inclusion: Disclosures for initial application of an Ind AS affecting periods
Disclosures for voluntary policy changes including justification and line-item adjustments
exclusion: Disclosures restricted strictly to routine changes in accounting estimates
nearby_distinctions: Differs from estimate change disclosures by focusing on transitional impacts, retrospective line-item adjustments, and standard titles rather than prospective operational effects.

descriptors.definition: Accounting estimates involve measurement uncertainty and require monetary amounts to be estimated using judgments or assumptions based on the latest available information. Modifications to these estimates arise from changes in underlying circumstances, new information, developments, or updated experience rather than prior period corrections.
inclusion: Adjustments to expected credit loss allowances
Revisions of inventory net realisable values or asset useful lives
exclusion: Corrections of mathematical mistakes or misinterpretations representing prior period errors
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from changes in accounting policies, which alter the core measurement basis or convention rather than adjusting uncertain monetary inputs.

descriptors.definition: Accounting estimates address measurement uncertainty where financial statement items cannot be directly observed and require monetary approximations using available reliable data. Utilizing reasonable estimates is foundational to preparing financial statements without compromising their overall reliability.
inclusion: Calculations involving direct estimation or valuation methodologies
Provisions, loss allowances, and depreciation parameters
nearby_distinctions: Differs from raw model inputs, which serve as foundational data components rather than the final output accounting estimate.

descriptors.concept_name: Distinction and Timing of Accounting Estimate Changes
descriptors.definition: Changes in accounting estimates stem from updated information or shifting operational contexts and do not represent prior period corrections. When distinguishing an accounting policy change from an estimate change proves difficult, the modification is treated as a change in estimate.
inclusion: Modifications driven by new operational experience or altered inputs
Ambiguous adjustments defaulting to estimate treatment
exclusion: Alterations to core measurement bases or inventory cost formulas, which constitute policy changes
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from policy changes by treating underlying principle modifications as policy shifts, while empirical or input updates are treated as estimates.

descriptors.concept_name: Change in Measurement Basis versus Estimate
descriptors.definition: A shift in the core measurement basis applied to financial statement items constitutes a change in accounting policy rather than an accounting estimate. In scenarios where differentiating between a policy change and an estimate change is problematic, the adjustment is classified as a change in accounting estimate.
inclusion: Shifting inventory cost formulas between FIFO and weighted average
Modifying fundamental accounting conventions
exclusion: Adjusting useful lives or loss allowance rates based on current experience
nearby_distinctions: Differs from estimate changes because measurement bases dictate the primary valuation framework rather than fine-tuning unobservable variables.

descriptors.concept_name: Accounting Treatment for Changes in Estimates
descriptors.definition: The financial impact of a change in an accounting estimate is recognized prospectively through profit or loss either in the current period alone or across current and future periods. If the change modifies assets, liabilities, or equity items, its effect is recognized directly by adjusting the carrying amount of the related item during the period of change.
inclusion: Prospective inclusion of estimate effects in profit or loss
Adjustments to asset, liability, or equity carrying amounts in the current period
exclusion: Retrospective restatement of prior period financial statements
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from prior period error corrections, which require retrospective restatement rather than prospective current and future period adjustments.

descriptors.concept_name: Disclosure of Changes in Accounting Estimates
descriptors.definition: An entity must disclose the specific nature and monetary amount of any accounting estimate change impacting the current period or expected future periods. If determining the future period impact is impracticable, the entity must explicitly disclose that limitation.
inclusion: Quantified impacts on current period results
Disclosures of anticipated future period effects or statements of impracticability
exclusion: Extensive retrospective transition disclosures required for accounting policy alterations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from policy change disclosures by omitting historical retrospective restatement breakdowns and focusing purely on current and prospective effects.

descriptors.definition: Prior period errors involve omissions or misstatements from past financial periods resulting from a failure to use or misuse of reliable information that was available and reasonably obtainable when financial statements were authorized. These errors encompass mathematical mistakes, policy application flaws, factual misinterpretations, and fraud.
inclusion: Mathematical calculation mistakes and wrong totals
Improper offsetting of receivables and payables breaching presentation rules
Misinterpretations of facts or post-reporting events
exclusion: Changes in estimates resulting from newly uncovered or evolving operational insights
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from changes in estimates because errors stem from failing to use available historical information, whereas estimates involve legitimate uncertainties at the time.

descriptors.concept_name: Meaning and Types of Prior Period Errors
descriptors.definition: Prior period errors represent past financial statement omissions or misstatements caused by misusing or ignoring reliable information that could have been obtained when reports were issued. Such discrepancies include computational errors, policy misapplications like improper offsetting, misinterpretations of facts, and fraudulent entries.
inclusion: Mathematical and calculation errors
Incorrect policy application such as unauthorized asset-liability offsetting
Misinterpretation of reporting period events
exclusion: Legitimate prospective adjustments driven by changing business circumstances
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from accounting estimate changes by representing factual oversights or data misuse of past information rather than updated judgments on uncertain future outcomes.
